newsitem.title: GERMANY: Preussag says Q1 steel orders, output up.
newsitem.headline: Preussag says Q1 steel orders, output up.

text.p: Preussag AG chairman Michael Frenzel said on Thursday prices, orders and output rose at steel unit Preussag Stahl in the first quarter of the current business year.
Orders were up 20 percent in the quarter ended December, while production rose 35 percent.
"Prices followed these trends only hesitantly, but we were able to to raise our prices in the first quarter," Frenzel said in remarks prepared for delivery at the company's annual news conference.
"We are sure that we are passed the low point in prices, but we cannot say how quickly the train will gather momentum," he said.
Frenzel said it was too early to give a solid earnings outlook for the steel sector. "The crucial factor will be whether we can implement the planned price increases."

In the year ended September 30, crude steel production in Germany shrank 10 percent, while world production fell only one percent. Output in Japan dropped five percent, and in the European Union eight percent, he said.
